edition.locus: On the Unity of the Church 8

source_text: Quis ergo sic est sceleratus et perfidus, quis sic discordiae furore vesanus, ut aut credat scindi posse aut audeat scindere unitatem Dei, vestem Domini, Ecclesiam Christi? Monet ipse in Evangelio suo et docet dicens: Et erit unus grex et unus pastor. Et esse posse uno in loco aliquis existimat aut multos pastores aut plures greges? Apostolus item Paulus, hanc eamdem nobis insinuans unitatem, obsecrat et hortatur dicens: Obsecro, inquit, vos, fratres, per nomen Domini nostri Jesu Christi, ut id ipsum dicatis omnes, et non sint in vobis schismata. Sitis autem compositi in eodem sensu et in eadem sententia. Et iterum dicit: Sustinentes invicem in dilectione, satis agentes servare unitatem spiritus in conjunctione pacis. Stare tu et vivere putas posse de Ecclesia recedentem, sedes sibi alias et diversa domicilia condentem, cum dictum sit ad Rahab, in qua praeformabatur Ecclesia: Patrem tuum et matrem tuam et fratres tuos et totam domum patris tui colliges ad te ipsam in domum tuam, et omnis qui exierit ostium domus tuae foras, reus sibi erit. Item sacramentum Paschae nihil aliud in Exodi lege contineat quam ut agnus, qui in figura Christi occiditur, in domo una edatur. Loquitur Deus dicens: In domo una comedetur, non ejicietis de domo carnem foras. Caro Christi et sanctum Domini ejici foras non potest, nec alia ulla credentibus praeter unam Ecclesiam domus est. Hanc domum, hoc unanimitatis hospitium designat et denuntiat Spiritus sanctus in Psalmis dicens: Deus qui inhabitare facit unanimes in domo. In domo Dei, in Ecclesia Christi, unanimes habitant, concordes et simplices perseverant.
pass_a_gloss: Who therefore is so wicked and faithless, who is so insane with the fury of discord, that he either believes that the unity of God can be torn apart or dares to tear apart the unity of God, the garment of the Lord, the Church of Christ? He himself warns in his Gospel and teaches, saying: And there will be one flock and one shepherd. And does anyone think that there can be one flock in one place or many shepherds or many flocks? The Apostle Paul also, indicating this same unity to us, begs and exhorts, saying: I beg you, brothers, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all say the same thing, and that there not be schisms among you. But be united in the same sense and in the same opinion. And again he says: Supporting one another in love, being sufficient to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace. Do you think that one who departs from the Church and establishes other seats and different dwellings for himself can stand and live, when it was said to Rahab, in whom the Church was prefigured: Gather your father and your mother and your brothers and your whole father's household to yourself into your house, and everyone who goes out of the door of your house outside will be guilty. Likewise, the sacrament of the Passover contains nothing else in the law of Exodus than that the lamb, which is killed in the figure of Christ, is eaten in one house. God speaks, saying: It will be eaten in one house, you will not throw the flesh outside the house. The flesh of Christ and the holy thing of the Lord cannot be thrown outside, nor is there any other house for believers except the one Church. The Holy Spirit designates and announces this house, this hospitality of unity, in the Psalms, saying: God who makes those who are of one mind dwell in a house. In the house of God, in the Church of Christ, those who are of one mind dwell, and they persevere, harmonious and simple.

pass_b_english: What kind of person would be so depraved and disloyal, so consumed by the madness of discord, as to think the unity of God can be torn apart or even dare to try to tear it apart - the unity that is the Church of Christ, the very garment of the Lord? In his Gospel, Christ himself teaches us that there will be one flock and one shepherd (John 10:16), which raises the question: can there be one flock with many shepherds, or multiple flocks in one place? The Apostle Paul urges us to unity, begging us in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to speak with one voice and avoid schisms (1 Corinthians 1:10), to be of the same mind and share the same opinion, and to support one another in love, working together to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace (Ephesians 4:3). Can someone who leaves the Church and sets up their own separate gatherings and meeting places really expect to stand and live? Consider the story of Rahab, who prefigured the Church: she was told to gather her family into her house, and anyone who left the house would be guilty (Joshua 2:18-19). The Passover sacrament, as described in the law of Exodus, also emphasizes unity: the lamb, which represents Christ, must be eaten in one house, and the flesh must not be taken outside (Exodus 12:46). This means the body of Christ, the holy thing of the Lord, cannot be taken outside, and there is no other place for believers to gather except the one Church. The Holy Spirit announces this unity, this hospitality, in the Psalms, saying that God brings like-minded people together in one house (Psalm 68:6), and it is in the house of God, in the Church of Christ, that those who are of one mind dwell, living in harmony and simplicity.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required inline scripture citations (John 10:16, 1 Corinthians 1:10, Ephesians 4:3, Joshua 2:18-19, Exodus 12:46, Psalm 68:6) which were alluded to in the Latin but not explicitly cited with verse numbers. Pass A is a faithful literal translation. All clauses, agency, and theological distinctions are preserved.
